'''Jestefad''' was a large [[gas giant]] [[planet]] located in the [[Atravis sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]'<ref name="CL" /> [[Western Reaches]] portion,<ref name="Location" /> in the [[Mustafar system]],<ref name="CL" /> at grid square L-19<ref name="TFABG" /> of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> In close [[orbit]] of its smaller twin world of [[Mustafar]], Jestefad's [[Gravity|gravitational]] field subjected the [[Volcano|volcanic]] planet to immense tidal forces, and its large electromagnetic field swamped the small [[Volcano|volcanic]] planet, which created wild electrical storms, and was constantly trying to make Mustafar into its [[moon]] with its gravity. However, influence from a further second gas giant, [[Lefrani]], pulled the smaller planet away from Jestefad, effectively turning Mustafar into an unstable world of [[magma]] and rock.<ref name="CL" /> Jestefad had a moon of its own, the [[ocean]] moon [[Nur]].<ref name="Devoted" />

Several [[Millennium|millennia]] ago, Jestefad and Lefrani were pulled out their orbit around the [[star]] [[Priate]] during a cataclysmic struggle between the [[Jedi]] and [[Sith]]. As a result, both were placed close to the smaller world of Mustafar, suspending the planet between their two gravitational pulls.<ref name="BMF 17" />

==Behind the scenes==
Jestefad first appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> which was released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].<ref name="ROTS date">{{SW|url=news/critical-opinion-revenge-of-the-sith-original-reviews|text=Critical Opinion: ''Revenge of the Sith'' Original Reviews}}</ref> The planet was first identified in new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 17|seventeeth]] issue of the ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'' magazine,<ref name="BMF 17" /> published around [[April 29]], [[2015]].<ref name="BMFdate">{{BMFdates|17}}</ref> [[Jestefad/Legends|Jestefad]] was first identified in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] in [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']], a reference book published by [[Dorling Kindersley]]<ref name="Complete Locations 2005">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'', 2005 edition]]</ref> on [[October 17]], 2005.<ref name="CL 2005 date">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/news20050314.html|text=DK: The Ultimate in ''Star Wars'' Guides}}</ref>

[[Star Wars Inside Intel|''Star Wars Inside Intel: The Inquisitorius'']] originally stated that Nur orbited the planet Mustafar.<ref name="Insider Intel old">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-the-inquisitorius|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: The Inquisitorius|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}} {{C|version archived on Janurary 20, 2023; content now replaced}}</ref> However, this was later edited in [[2023]] to more vaguely state it was part of the Mustafar system.<ref name="Insider Intel">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-the-inquisitorius|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: The Inquisitorius|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}}</ref> Later that year,<ref name="DK UK">{{DK|url=uk/book/9780241666371-star-wars-dawn-of-rebellion-the-visual-guide|text=Star Wars Dawn of Rebellion The Visual Guide}}</ref> ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' would once again place Nur as orbiting Mustafar.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> However, the episode "[[Devoted]]" of ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Empire]]'' shows Nur orbiting Jestefad, with Mustafar visible in the background.<ref name="Devoted" /> This is supported by a [[hologram]] in "[[Part IV]]" of ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'' showing Nur's orbit around a planet that is not Mustafar.<ref name="K4">{{Kenobi|Part IV}}</ref>
